def _leading_adjunct_positions(tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace], verb: TokenTrace) -> set:
    """Positions of a LEADING ADJUNCT — a sentence-initial phrase set off by a comma BEFORE the main-clause
    subject ("Angered by the insult, the king banished …" / "Consumed by ambition, Macbeth murders …") — to
    drop, so the real subject survives instead of the adjunct's head contaminating the agent.

    A capitalized sentence-initial participle ("Angered", "Consumed", "Exhausted") is POS-tagged PROPN, so it
    is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a proper-noun subject by tag; the reliable signal is the COMMA — the syntactic
    boundary English uses for a fronted adjunct (participial/absolute/adverbial). The subject is the nominal
    AFTER the last pre-verb comma; everything from sentence start up to that comma is the leading adjunct.

    Conservative guards, so a comma is not over-read: fire only when (a) a subject-eligible nominal (NOUN/
    PROPN) actually follows the last pre-verb comma, and (b) that following span carries NO coordinator — so a
    comma-separated LIST subject ("Tom, Dick and Harry ran") stays whole (there the coordinator sits AFTER the
    comma, whereas in a coordinated leading adjunct "Consumed by X and spurred by Y, Macbeth …" it sits
    BEFORE). The subject-initial appositive ("Haemon, Creon's son, pledged") has NO nominal after its last
    comma, so this abstains and `_appositive_positions` handles it — the two are disjoint by construction."""
    pre = sorted([t for t in tokens if t.position < verb.position], key=lambda t: t.position)
    commas = [i for i, t in enumerate(pre) if t.pos == "PUNCT" and t.lemma == ","]
    if not commas:
        return set()
    after = pre[commas[-1] + 1 :]  # tokens between the last pre-verb comma and the verb
    if not any(t.pos in ("NOUN", "PROPN") for t in after):
        return set()  # no subject after the comma -> not a fronted adjunct
    if any(t.lemma in ("and", "or") for t in after):
        return set()  # coordinator after the comma -> a list subject, keep it
    return {t.position for t in pre[: commas[-1]]}
def _select_clause_verb(tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace]):
    """The clause's predicate verb. Normally the first eligible VERB (non-copula, non-operator).

    LEADING-ADJUNCT override (the verb twin of `_leading_adjunct_positions`): a coordinated/fronted
    PARTICIPLE inside a leading adjunct is POS=VERB and comes first ("Consumed by X and spurred by Y,
    Macbeth murders …" → `spur` before `murder`), so the naive first-VERB pick takes the adjunct's verb.
    The signal that the first verb is adjunct-internal: it is NOT immediately preceded by its own subject
    (a bare PROPN/NOUN/PRON). When that holds AND a later verb sits after a comma with a subject before it
    (the real main clause), that later verb is the predicate. A TRAILING adjunct ("Macbeth fled, fearing
    capture") is untouched — its first verb IS preceded by its subject "Macbeth", so the override abstains."""
    by_pos = sorted(tokens, key=lambda t: t.position)
    eligible = [t for t in by_pos if t.pos == "VERB" and t.lemma != _COPULA_LEMMA and not t.is_operator]
    if not eligible:
        return None
    v1 = eligible[0]
    before_v1 = [t for t in by_pos if t.position < v1.position]
    if before_v1 and before_v1[-1].pos in _SUBJECT_POS:
        return v1  # v1 preceded by its subject -> main/trailing verb
    comma = next((t.position for t in by_pos if t.pos == "PUNCT" and t.lemma == "," and t.position > v1.position), None)
    if comma is None:
        return v1
    for v2 in eligible:
        if v2.position > comma and any(comma < n.position < v2.position and n.pos in _SUBJECT_POS for n in by_pos):
            return v2  # a later verb whose subject sits after the adjunct comma
    return v1
def _try_event(
    tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace], shared_subject: Optional[Sequence] = None, signs: Optional[Signs] = None
) -> Optional[Expression]:
    """Synthesize an EVENT ``Op`` from a plain verb clause "X verbs Y".

    The base case the operator set was missing: a clause with an ordinary content
    verb (not the copula "be", not a COMP_* operator token) and no other
    operator. Mirrors :func:`_try_copula_type_assertion` — the verb is detected by
    POS (so it works for sub-clause verbs that aren't the sentence ROOT, e.g. the
    ``became`` of "…because Duncan became happy"); subject = tokens before it,
    object/complement = tokens after. Returns ``None`` when no content verb is
    present, so callers fall through to the default phrase build.

    The verb lemma rides on ``Op.primitive``; ``operators.event`` reads it back.
    """
    verb = _select_clause_verb(tokens)
    if verb is None:
        return None
    # Clausal negation ("X does not harm Y"): NOT is a sign-direction argument
    # (sentence_architecture.md), so drop the marker from the argument spans and
    # wrap the synthesized EVENT in a Negation — the same node the in-span path
    # (_build_arg_expression) and the emitter already understand. Only a sign that
    # lands on this event's own verb or participants: "I think this doesn't work"
    # does not negate think, and "He left not because…" negates the because.
    negated = _takes_sign(tokens, _sign_owners(tokens) if signs is None else signs, verb.position)
    _ordered = sorted(tokens, key=lambda t: t.position)

    def _prep_governed(tok) -> bool:
        """Is ``tok`` the object of a preposition? Walk back over its own determiner/adjective
        premodifiers (only — NOT other nominals, so a fronted PP's object is not confused with
        the following subject head); if the governing token is a preposition, ``tok`` is a PP
        oblique. Catches a FRONTED adverbial before the subject ("In the daytime I ran" →
        daytime governed, I not) — the subject-side twin of the post-verb object/oblique split,
        so a fronted PP no longer blobs into the subject ("daytime i"). Text-agnostic.

        EXCEPTION — a genitive/territorial ``of``-postmodifier of a preceding NAME/head-NOUN
        ("Richard of Gloucester", "Duncan of Scotland", "the son of Duncan") is PART of that
        nominal, not a fronted PP: its object stays with the subject rather than being peeled off
        as a SYN_OBL (which `event()` then mis-reads as a `theme`). Restricted to ``of`` (the
        genitive connector) so an adverbial PP after the subject head ("Macbeth in his rage …")
        stays an oblique. This is PRE-verb only; a real imputed-act complement ("accuses Y OF
        treason") is post-verb and split by the object/oblique boundary below, so it is untouched."""
        for t in reversed([x for x in _ordered if x.position < tok.position]):
            if t.pos in ("DET", "ADJ"):
                continue
            if t.pos != "ADP":
                return False
            if t.lemma == "of":
                for u in reversed([x for x in _ordered if x.position < t.position]):
                    if u.pos in ("DET", "ADJ"):
                        continue
                    return u.pos not in ("PROPN", "NOUN")  # head noun before "of" -> postmodifier -> keep
            return True
        return False

    appositive = _appositive_positions(tokens, verb)  # NAME, description, → keep the name (Haemon)
    leading_adjunct = _leading_adjunct_positions(tokens, verb)  # "Angered by X, the king …" → keep the king
    subject_tokens = [
        t
        for t in tokens
        if t.position < verb.position
        and t.pos != "PUNCT"
        and t.lemma not in _NEGATION_LEMMAS
        and not _prep_governed(t)
        and t.position not in appositive
        and t.position not in leading_adjunct
    ]
    # A nominalized-adjective subject ("A giant attacks", "A stranger helps") is the NP head used as a
    # noun; promote it so it grounds as the agent instead of being dropped as a bare adjective atom.
    subject_atoms = _promote_nominalized_adjective_subject(
        subject_tokens, [_atom_from_token(t) for t in subject_tokens]
    )
    # Appositive type-inheritance (hint only — the thread is filled at the grounding annotate seam): when
    # the subject is a NAME described by an appositive ("Arjun, a warrior" / "Haemon, Creon's son"), carry
    # the description's head noun onto the kept proper-noun atom. The name stays the agent (this does not
    # touch subject selection); grounding later types it from what the TEXT says when the name itself can't
    # be placed. The apposition head is the LAST noun of the dropped appositive span.
    if appositive:
        _appos_nouns = [
            t
            for t in sorted(tokens, key=lambda t: t.position)
            if t.position in appositive and t.pos in ("NOUN", "PROPN")
        ]
        if _appos_nouns:
            _ah = _appos_nouns[-1].lemma
            subject_atoms = [replace(a, apposition=_ah) if a.pos == "PROPN" else a for a in subject_atoms]
    fronted_obliques = [
        _atom_from_token(t, "SYN_OBL")
        for t in tokens
        if t.position < verb.position and t.pos != "PUNCT" and t.lemma not in _NEGATION_LEMMAS and _prep_governed(t)
    ]
    # Direct object vs PP obliques. The clause's direct object is the post-verb nominal
    # span UP TO the first preposition; tokens from the first preposition on are PP
    # obliques ("for months", "with this result", "to Macbeth"). Without this split the
    # object accretes every trailing PP nominal into one blobbed entity (the demi-word
    # span — "penny she month this result"). The obliques are RESOLVED as a typed
    # SYN_OBL constituent rather than merged or discarded; the narrative spine's
    # set-operation keeps them off the protagonist backbone. (Text-agnostic: the boundary
    # is the preposition POS, not any story-specific word.)
    post_verb = [
        t for t in tokens if t.position > verb.position and t.pos != "PUNCT" and t.lemma not in _NEGATION_LEMMAS
    ]
    first_prep = next((idx for idx, t in enumerate(post_verb) if t.pos == "ADP"), None)
    obj_tokens = post_verb if first_prep is None else post_verb[:first_prep]
    obl_tokens = [] if first_prep is None else post_verb[first_prep:]
    object_atoms = [_atom_from_token(t) for t in obj_tokens]
    oblique_atoms = fronted_obliques + [_atom_from_token(t, "SYN_OBL") for t in obl_tokens]
    if not subject_atoms:
        # VP-coordination with an elided shared subject ("Bertran [betrayed Aldric] and
        # [murdered him]") — inherit the prior conjunct's subject so the 2nd event survives
        # instead of collapsing to its bare object. Only fires when the clause has no subject.
        if not shared_subject:
            return None
        subject_atoms = list(shared_subject)
    args: List[Operand] = [Phrase(atoms=subject_atoms)]
    if object_atoms:
        args.append(Phrase(atoms=object_atoms))
        # Carry obliques only BEHIND a real object, so a bare PP after an intransitive
        # ("stood by the window") never slides into the patient slot (args[1]).
        if oblique_atoms:
            args.append(Phrase(atoms=oblique_atoms))
    # A modal auxiliary before the verb ("might", "can", "must") qualifies the event, keyed on its primes (#66).
    modal = modal_primes([t.word_primitives for t in tokens if t.position < verb.position and t.pos == "AUX"])
    event = Op(primitive=verb.lemma, operation="EVENT", arity=len(args), args=args, modal=modal)
    # A bare post-verbal PP qualifies the event; it is not the verb's direct
    # patient. Use the existing relation-over-event representation (also used
    # for unresolved nominal prepositions), preserving BOTH the preposition
    # and its anchor. Previously these constituents were silently discarded
    # just because there was no object to put before them in EVENT.args.
    if not object_atoms and len(obl_tokens) > 1:
        event = Op(
            primitive=obl_tokens[0].lemma,
            operation="EVENT",
            arity=2,
            args=[event, Phrase(atoms=[_atom_from_token(t, "SYN_OBL") for t in obl_tokens[1:]])],
        )
    return Negation(operand=event) if negated else event
def _clause_core(tokens, shared_subject, signs):
    """Build the recoverable clause before a qualifying operator is attached."""
    content, duration = split_duration(tokens)
    if duration is not None and split_duration(content)[1] is None:
        qualified = _clause_core(content, shared_subject, signs)
        core, negations = _unwrap_negations(qualified)
        if isinstance(core, Op) and core.operation in {"EVENT", "TYPE_ASSERT"}:
            return _rewrap_negations(replace(core, duration=duration), negations)
    temporal = _nominal_temporal_attachment(tokens)
    if temporal is not None:
        content, linker, anchor, operation = temporal
        return Op(
            primitive=linker.lemma.upper() if operation == "TEMPORAL" else linker.lemma,
            operation=operation,
            arity=2,
            args=[_clause_core(content, shared_subject, signs), Phrase(atoms=[_atom_from_token(t) for t in anchor])],
        )
    copula = _try_copula_type_assertion(tokens, signs)
    if copula is not None:
        return _with_clause_modal(copula, tokens)
    event = _try_event(tokens, shared_subject=shared_subject, signs=signs)
    if event is not None:
        return event
    atoms = [_atom_from_token(t) for t in tokens if t.lemma not in _NEGATION_LEMMAS or t.pos in {"NOUN", "PRON"}]
    core = atoms[0] if len(atoms) == 1 else Phrase(atoms=atoms)
    return Negation(operand=core) if _takes_sign(tokens, signs) else core
def _build_clause_expr(
    clause: ClauseSpan,
    tokens: Sequence[TokenTrace],
    operators: Sequence[OperatorTrace],
    operator_positions: Sequence[int],
    excluded: Optional[set] = None,
    drop_relativizers: bool = False,
    shared_subject: Optional[Sequence] = None,
    signs: Optional[Signs] = None,
) -> Expression:
    """Build the Expression for one clause span.

    A clause resolves through the *existing* single-clause logic: its
    within-clause operators (if any) are built and left-folded; otherwise the
    clause's content tokens fold into a copula TYPE_ASSERT or a Phrase / Atom.

    ``excluded`` token positions are dropped (an embedded child clause's tokens
    are excluded from the parent). ``drop_relativizers`` strips a leading
    who/which/that pronoun — used when building a relative clause's restriction.
    ``signs`` is the sentence's negation landings (:func:`_sign_owners`).
    """
    signs = _sign_owners(tokens) if signs is None else signs
    excluded = excluded or set()
    clause_tokens = [
        t
        for t in tokens
        if clause.token_start <= t.position < clause.token_end
        and t.position not in excluded
        and not (drop_relativizers and _is_relativizer(t))
    ]
    clause_ops = [operators[i] for i in clause.operator_indices]

    if not clause_ops:
        return _clause_core(clause_tokens, shared_subject, signs)

    for index in sorted(clause.operator_indices, key=lambda i: operators[i].position):
        op = operators[index]
        left = [t for t in clause_tokens if t.position < op.position]
        right = [t for t in clause_tokens if t.position > op.position]
        left_pred = any(t.pos == "VERB" or (t.pos == "AUX" and t.lemma == "be") for t in left if not t.is_operator)
        right_pred = any(t.pos == "VERB" or (t.pos == "AUX" and t.lemma == "be") for t in right if not t.is_operator)
        head = not any(t.pos not in ("PUNCT", "CCONJ", "SCONJ") for t in left)
        plan = operator_composition_plan(op.operation, op.arity, left_pred, right_pred, head)
        remaining = [i for i in clause.operator_indices if i != index]
        args: List[Operand]
        duration = None
        if plan == "clause_pair":
            operand_exclusions = excluded
            if op.operation == "TEMPORAL":
                duration, offset_positions = temporal_offset(clause_tokens, op.position)
                operand_exclusions = excluded | offset_positions
            before = replace(
                clause,
                token_end=op.position,
                operator_indices=[i for i in remaining if operators[i].position < op.position],
            )
            after = replace(
                clause,
                token_start=op.position + 1,
                operator_indices=[i for i in remaining if operators[i].position > op.position],
            )
            args = [
                _build_clause_expr(
                    before,
                    tokens,
                    operators,
                    operator_positions,
                    operand_exclusions,
                    drop_relativizers,
                    shared_subject,
                    signs,
                ),
                _build_clause_expr(
                    after, tokens, operators, operator_positions, excluded, drop_relativizers, shared_subject, signs
                ),
            ]
        elif plan in ("qualified_core", "open_discourse"):
            inner_clause = replace(clause, operator_indices=remaining)
            core = _build_clause_expr(
                inner_clause,
                tokens,
                operators,
                operator_positions,
                excluded | {op.position},
                drop_relativizers,
                shared_subject,
                signs,
            )
            args = [Phrase(atoms=[]), core] if plan == "open_discourse" else [core]
        elif plan == "matrix_core":
            event = _try_event(clause_tokens, shared_subject=shared_subject, signs=signs)
            if event is not None:
                return event
            continue
        else:
            continue
        built = Op(
            primitive=_operator_primitive(op, clause_tokens),
            operation=op.operation,
            arity=len(args),
            args=args,
            duration=duration,
        )
        return Negation(operand=built) if op.position in _negated_operators(signs) else built

    built = [_build_operator_op(op, tokens, operator_positions, signs) for op in clause_ops]
    if len(built) == 1:
        return built[0]
    return _left_fold_operators(built)

def set_restrict(op: Op) -> SetRestriction:
    """COMP_ONLY / SET_RESTRICT — restrict set to lone member.

    User spec: "Only X [predicate]" → ∀Y: predicate(Y) → Y = X. The
    arity-1 arg is the lone member; the predicate is the surrounding
    sentence context. For v1 we represent the predicate as the Op's
    arg with a note that the surrounding context is implicit.
    """
    _require_min_arity(op, 1)
    core = op.args[0]
    content = core.operand if isinstance(core, Negation) else core
    member = (
        content.agent if isinstance(content, Event) else content.entity if isinstance(content, TypeAssertion) else core
    )
    return SetRestriction(member=member, predicate=core)
def scalar_extreme(op: Op) -> BoundaryCase:
    """COMP_EVEN / SCALAR_EXTREME — v1 inert placeholder.

    Per user decision 2026-05-23: not a 1st-order primitive. Records the
    operation without asserting the scalar-extreme universal. Deferred
    to future hierarchical-network-traversal work.
    """
    _require_min_arity(op, 1)
    core = op.args[0]
    content = core.operand if isinstance(core, Negation) else core
    entity = (
        content.agent if isinstance(content, Event) else content.entity if isinstance(content, TypeAssertion) else core
    )
    return BoundaryCase(entity=entity, predicate=core)
def control(op: Op) -> Control:
    """CONTROL — controller entity carries out the inner infinitival clause.

    "Mike wants to leave" → ``Control(controller=Mike, inner=leave)``.
    Synthesized in ``from_trace`` from an embedded control ClauseSpan; arity=2,
    arg0 = the controller entity, arg1 = the inner clause's content.
    """
    if op.arity >= 3:
        return Control(
            controller=op.args[1],
            inner=op.args[2],
            verb=op.primitive,
            subject=op.args[0],
            modal=op.modal,
            duration=op.duration,
        )
    _require_arity(op, 2)  # degraded fall-back (non-Event matrix)
    return Control(controller=op.args[0], inner=op.args[1], modal=op.modal, duration=op.duration)
def event(op: Op) -> Event:
    """EVENT — a verb roleframe over its arguments (the base-case predicate).

    "Duncan rewarded Macbeth" → ``Event(verb="reward", agent=duncan,
    patient=macbeth)``. Synthesized in ``from_trace`` from a plain verb clause;
    the verb lemma rides on ``Op.primitive``, arg0 = subject, arg1 = object (when
    present, else intransitive).
    """
    if not op.args:
        raise ValueError(f"EVENT expects ≥1 arg, got {op.arity}")
    # Args beyond agent+patient are the SECONDARY constituents the role-split peeled off a
    # ditransitive / object+complement (resolution's ArgSplit flattened them in). Preserve
    # them as latent `themes` — the clean primary read (agent, patient) is unchanged; themes
    # ride along, dropped from the default analysis but revivable.
    return Event(
        verb=op.primitive,
        agent=op.args[0],
        patient=op.args[1] if len(op.args) > 1 else None,
        themes=tuple(op.args[2:]) if len(op.args) > 2 else (),
        modal=op.modal,
        duration=op.duration,
    )
def temporal(op: Op) -> Temporal:
    """TEMPORAL — when/while/after/before X, Y → both clauses asserted, temporal link.

    Like CAUSAL_SOURCE / IMPLIES, the *subordinate* (when-)clause is the arg1/right
    operand in both readings — "Y when X" (medial) and "When X, Y" (fronted, where the
    encoder presents the clauses as ``[main, dependent]``). So the when-clause is always
    the setting: setting = arg1, event = arg0.
    """
    _require_arity(op, 2)
    conjunction = op.primitive.lower() if op.primitive in ("BEFORE", "AFTER") else "when"
    return Temporal(
        setting=op.args[1],
        event=op.args[0],
        conjunction=op.duration.relation if op.duration else conjunction,
        duration=op.duration,
    )
def evaluate_tree(expr: Operand):
    """Walk an Expression tree, evaluating every Op into a Predicate.

    Returns:
        Either an unchanged leaf (Atom, Phrase, Negation of leaf) or a
        Predicate (for Op nodes). Nested Ops are evaluated recursively:
        each Op's args are evaluated before the Op itself, so the result
        is a tree of Predicates with Expression leaves.
    """
    if isinstance(expr, Op):
        # Recurse into args first so nested Ops become Predicates before
        # the parent dispatch sees them.
        evaluated_args = [evaluate_tree(a) for a in expr.args]
        return evaluate(replace(expr, args=evaluated_args))
    if isinstance(expr, Negation):
        # Preserve the sign around WHATEVER the operand evaluates to — including a
        # Predicate (a negated event/type-assertion, "X does not harm Y"). The old
        # guard kept the wrapper only around leaves/Ops and dropped it for
        # Predicates, silently losing clausal negation; emit_contract already
        # turns a Negation(Predicate) into {"op": "NOT", ...}.
        return Negation(operand=evaluate_tree(expr.operand))
    if isinstance(expr, Coordination):
        return replace(expr, members=tuple(evaluate_tree(member) for member in expr.members))
    return expr

    | _CCONJ
    | _SCONJ
    | _AUX_BE
    | _AUX_MODAL
    | _AUX_DO
    | _PART
    | _ADV_CLOSED
    | {"there", "here", "then", "now"}
)
def _pos(self, surf: str, i: int, surfaces: List[str]) -> str:
        low = surf.lower()
        previous = surfaces[i - 1] if i > 0 else ""
        prev = previous.lower() if isinstance(previous, str) else ""
        if _PUNCT_RE.fullmatch(surf):
            return "PUNCT"
        if surf.replace(",", "").replace(".", "").isdigit():
            return "NUM"
        if (
            low in _AUX_MODAL
            and i > 0
            and (surfaces[i - 1].lower() in _POSS_PRON or surfaces[i - 1].lower() in ("the", "a", "an"))
        ):
            # A modal homograph right after an article or possessive is the NOUN, not the modal:
            # "makes his will" / "opened the can". A SUBJECT pronoun ("he will go") is not in this
            # set, so the modal reading is preserved. Without this, "will" tagged AUX is dropped as a
            # function word and "his will" collapses to the bare possessor (make(alonso, alonso)).
            return "NOUN"
        if low in _AUX_BE or low in _AUX_MODAL or low in _AUX_DO:
            return "AUX"
        if low in _NT_STEM and i + 1 < len(surfaces) and surfaces[i + 1].lower() == "n't":
            return "AUX"
        if low in ("has", "have", "had", "'ve"):
            # Perfect auxiliary ("had murdered Duncan") vs main/possessive verb ("had a
            # crown"): a determiner/pronoun/preposition next → the main verb; a verb
            # (the participle) next → the perfect auxiliary. Scan past intervening
            # adverbs/negation ("had never murdered"). Without this, "had" was tagged
            # VERB and stole the predicate slot, dropping the real verb (have(x,y)).
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(surfaces) and (surfaces[j].lower().endswith("ly") or surfaces[j].lower() in _NEG):
                j += 1
            nxt = surfaces[j].lower() if j < len(surfaces) else ""
            if nxt in _DET or nxt in _PRON or nxt in _POSS_PRON or nxt in _ADP:
                return "VERB"
            return "AUX" if self._looks_verbal(nxt) else "VERB"
        if low in _NEG:
            return "PART"
        if low == "to":
            # infinitival 'to' (next is a verb) → PART, else preposition.
            nxt = surfaces[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(surfaces) else ""
            return "PART" if self._looks_verbal(nxt) else "ADP"
        if low in _POSS_PRON:
            return "PRON"
        if low in _DET and low not in _PRON:
            return "DET"
        if low in _PRON and low != "that":
            return "PRON"
        if low in _CCONJ:
            return "CCONJ"
        if low in _SCONJ and low not in ("that",):
            return "SCONJ"
        if low == "that":
            # 'that' is genuinely 3-way (DET/SCONJ/PRON); resolved by enumerate-and-score,
            # not the _PRON trap above (excluded) nor a next-token rule.
            return self._resolve_that(i, surfaces)
        if low == "than":
            return "ADP"
        if low in _ADP:
            return "ADP"
        if low == "'s":
            return "PART"
        # Closed-class adverb / connective / deictic adverb — no entity reading; tag ADV
        # before the open-class WordNet/title-case logic that was mis-promoting these to
        # NOUN/PROPN and then to AGENT. (See _ADV_CLOSED.)
        if copula_degree_reading(low, prev in _DET or prev in _POSS_PRON) == "DEGREE_ADV":
            return "ADV"
        if low in _ADV_CLOSED:
            return "ADV"

        # --- open class ----------------------------------------------------
        # Title-case alphabetic non-stop word → proper noun (the register's
        # names: Macbeth/Mike/Rex/Spot/Lady — incl. sentence-initial).
        if surf.isalpha() and surf.istitle() and low not in _STOP:
            at_head = i == 0 or previous in (".", "!", "?")
            nxt = surfaces[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(surfaces) else ""
            # Capitalization at a sentence boundary is orthographic evidence.
            # A known verb followed by a nominal opener is an imperative;
            # an adverb before a boundary retains its discourse reading.
            if at_head and wn.synsets(low, pos="v") and nxt in (_DET | _POSS_PRON | _PRON):
                return "VERB"
            if at_head and wn.synsets(low, pos="r") and nxt in (",", ".", "!", "?"):
                return "ADV"
            return "PROPN"

        senses = [wn.synsets(low, pos=pos) for pos in ("v", "n", "a", "s", "r")]
        mv = wn.morphy(low, "v") or ""
        has_v = bool(senses[0] or mv)
        has_n = bool(senses[1])
        has_a = bool(senses[2] or senses[3])
        has_r = bool(senses[4])
        closed_nonverbs = _NEG | _ADV_CLOSED | _ADV_DEGREE | _DET | _PRON | _POSS_PRON | _ADP | _CCONJ | _SCONJ
        participle_kind = copula_participle_kind(
            low,
            mv,
            has_v,
            low in closed_nonverbs,
        )
        next_kind = "NOT_PARTICIPLE"
        if i + 1 < len(surfaces):
            nxt = surfaces[i + 1].lower()
            next_senses = [wn.synsets(nxt, pos=pos) for pos in ("v", "n", "a", "s", "r")]
            next_mv = wn.morphy(nxt, "v") or ""
            next_kind = copula_participle_kind(
                nxt,
                next_mv,
                bool(next_senses[0] or next_mv),
                nxt in closed_nonverbs,
            )
        modifier_context = copula_modifier_context(
            low,
            has_a,
            has_r,
            next_kind,
        )
        left_roles = []
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0:
            left = surfaces[j].lower()
            left_previous = surfaces[j - 1].lower() if j > 0 else ""
            left_a = wn.synsets(left, pos="a")
            left_s = wn.synsets(left, pos="s")
            role = copula_left_role(
                left,
                left_previous,
                bool(left_a or left_s),
                left in _AUX_BE,
                left in _NEG,
            )
            left_roles.append(role)
            if role != "SKIP":
                break
            j -= 1
        left_roles.reverse()
        reading = copula_complement_reading(
            left_roles,
            participle_kind == "PARTICIPLE",
            modifier_context == "MODIFIER",
            has_a,
            has_n,
        )
        if reading == "ADJ":
            return "ADJ"
        if reading == "NOUN":
            return "NOUN"

        # A complete bare gerund can name an activity in a nominal copula,
        # rather than describe an agent doing it ("occupation is teaching").
        # Demand a positive native IS-A path from the gerund noun to the
        # subject's activity reading, not merely a shared broad ancestor.
        # This licenses a nominal construction, not a lexical bank or a
        # claim that abstract things cannot act. Animate/mixed subjects,
        # objects, and following modifiers keep the progressive available.
        be_index = i - 1
        while be_index >= 0 and surfaces[be_index].lower() in _NEG:
            be_index -= 1
        if low.endswith("ing") and has_n and be_index >= 1 and surfaces[be_index].lower() in _AUX_BE:
            subject = wn.synsets(surfaces[be_index - 1].lower(), pos="n")

            def has_ancestor(synset, name):
                return any(item.name() == name for path in synset.hypernym_paths() for item in path)

            complete = all(_PUNCT_RE.fullmatch(item) for item in surfaces[i + 1 :])
            if (
                complete
                and subject
                and all(has_ancestor(s, "abstraction.n.06") for s in subject)
                and any(
                    has_ancestor(s, "act.n.02") and has_ancestor(gerund, s.name())
                    for s in subject
                    for gerund in senses[1]
                )
            ):
                return "NOUN"

        # A determined copular NP can have adjective modifiers between its
        # article and head. Its attested noun head is not a finite -s verb
        # ("is an inert gas"). This is occurrence grammar, not sense choice;
        # a noun/verb elsewhere and an article-less participle remain eligible
        # for their ordinary predicate readings.
        if has_n:
            j = i - 1
            while (
                j >= 0
                and surfaces[j].lower() not in _STOP
                and (
                    surfaces[j].lower() in _ADV_DEGREE
                    or wn.synsets(surfaces[j].lower(), pos="a")
                    or wn.synsets(surfaces[j].lower(), pos="s")
                )
            ):
                j -= 1
            if j < i - 1 and j >= 1 and surfaces[j].lower() in {"a", "an", "the"}:
                k = j - 1
                while k >= 0 and surfaces[k].lower() in (_NEG | _COPULA_SKIP):
                    k -= 1
                next_word = surfaces[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(surfaces) else ""
                at_nominal_end = (
                    not next_word or bool(_PUNCT_RE.fullmatch(next_word)) or next_word in (_ADP | _SCONJ | _CCONJ)
                )
                if k >= 0 and surfaces[k].lower() in _AUX_BE and at_nominal_end:
                    return "NOUN"

        if low.endswith("ly") and low != "only":
            return "ADV"

        # A *demonstrative-or-relativizer* "that" before this word is NOT a determiner context:
        # "the king that FELL" / "the sword that Macbeth HELD" — the verb after a relativizer
        # "that" must stay a verb, not be nominalized like the head of "that DOG". (When "that"
        # really is a determiner, the following word is a noun, which `has_n` tags NOUN anyway.)
        prev_det = (prev in _DET or prev in _POSS_PRON) and prev != "that"

        # An isolated content word with a verb reading is the predicate (no
        # object-position context to make it a noun) — matches spaCy's default
        # for single-token input and keeps a lemma's forms POS-consistent.
        if len(surfaces) == 1 and has_v and not has_a:
            return "VERB"

        # Inflectional morphology beats a noun sense, except right after an article or a possessive, where the word
        # opens or modifies a noun phrase ("the meaning", "a dividing cell") rather than being the predicate.
        if low.endswith(("ing", "ed")):
            nxt = surfaces[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(surfaces) else ""
            next_is_noun = bool(nxt) and nxt not in _STOP and bool(wn.synsets(nxt, pos="n"))
            prev_kind = "np_opener" if prev in _NP_OPENER else "other"
            return _inflected_pos(prev_kind, has_v, has_n, has_a, next_is_noun)
        # Irregular past / participle: morphy maps to a *different* verb lemma
        # (sang→sing, left→leave, saw→see) — a verb even when also a noun. But a
        # determiner/possessive in front forces the nominal reading when the word
        # has a noun sense (``the dove``=the bird, not past-of-dive; ``the saw``=the
        # tool): a finite-verb position settles it, exactly as for the morphy-opaque
        # table below. The ``-s`` forms are excluded here (handled positionally below).
        if mv and mv != low and not low.endswith("s") and not (has_n and prev_det):
            return "VERB"
        # Morphy-opaque irregular past (fell/rose/…): a finite-verb position settles it.
        if low in _IRREGULAR_PAST_VERB and not prev_det:
            return "VERB"
        if low.endswith(("ous", "ful", "less", "ive", "able", "ible")):
            return "ADJ"
        # Comparative / superlative (incl. suppletive better/best/worse): the
        # morphology operation is the single source of truth for "is this a degree
        # form?". A grounded degree form is an ADJ — except in clearly verbal position
        # (after a modal/do/neg/"to"), where a homographic verb wins ("will best
        # them"). Subsumes the old -er/-est heuristic and also catches the suppletives.
        if resolve_degree(low) is not None and not (
            prev in _AUX_MODAL or prev in _AUX_DO or prev in _NEG or prev == "to"
        ):
            return "ADJ"

        # Positional disambiguation relative to the verb-inventory.
        if (prev in _AUX_DO or prev in _AUX_MODAL or prev in _NEG or prev == "to") and has_v:
            return "VERB"  # content word after do/modal/neg/to
        # Predicate by exclusion: a verb-capable word right after a nominative SUBJECT pronoun
        # ("I know", "they think", "he wants") is the clause predicate — the subject slot is
        # filled and the predicate is the only role left to assign, so a stray noun sense
        # (know/think/want all have one) must not strand the clause verb-less.
        if prev in _SUBJ_PRON and has_v:
            return "VERB"
        # Pre-nominal adjective: a determiner-preceded word that is adjectival AND is
        # followed by a noun head is a modifier, not the NP head — "the old king" → old
        # is ADJ (king is the head), not the nominalized "the old". Without this, an adj
        # with a noun sense (old/young/rich/poor/great…) was tagged NOUN before the head,
        # garbling the NP ("old king" as one unit). Guards the DET→NOUN rule below.
        nxt = surfaces[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(surfaces) else ""
        if prev_det and has_a and nxt and nxt not in _STOP and bool(wn.synsets(nxt, pos="n")):
            return "ADJ"
        if prev_det and has_n:
            return "NOUN"  # head of a determined NP
        if low.endswith("s") and has_v and not low.endswith("ss") and prev not in _ADP:
            return "VERB"  # 3sg present (barks, murders, falls); but the
            # object of a preposition is nominal ("of sticks")
        # Adverb in modifier position: a word with a WordNet adverb sense, not in a determined
        # nominal slot, not a preposition's object, and not clause-initial, modifies the
        # predicate — "loved him much", "go far", "ran away" — rather than being a second
        # object/the subject. Determined ("the well"), PP ("of much"), copula-complement, and
        # subject-initial nominal uses were all settled by the rules above, so reaching here
        # with an adverb sense means the modifier reading. Keeps degree/quantity adverbs out
        # of the object span (they were defaulting to NOUN via the has_n fallback below).
        if has_r and not prev_det and prev not in _ADP and i > 0:
            return "ADV"

        # A complete bare degree phrase provides adjective context even without
        # a copula. Use the existing adjective inventory, not lexical bank
        # values, and leave determined NPs, following noun heads, prepositional
        # complements and intervening operators to their existing readings.
        # This selects a grammatical category, never an individual word sense.
        if has_a and i > 0 and all(_PUNCT_RE.fullmatch(item) for item in surfaces[i + 1 :]):
            prefix = [item.lower() for item in surfaces[:i] if item.lower() not in _NEG]
            encodings = [get_hierarchy_encoding(item.upper()) for item in prefix]
            if encodings and all(encoding and encoding[0] == "INTENSITY" for encoding in encodings):
                return "ADJ"

        if has_n:
            return "NOUN"
        if has_v:
            return "VERB"
        if has_a:
            return "ADJ"
        return "NOUN"
